notes:
Tapping something to look at it now actually opens it. A bill on an expense, a candidate's resume, an offer or appointment letter, a document somebody has submitted — all of these used to hand you a share sheet asking which app to send the file to, which is no help when you were only trying to read it. They now open in whatever your phone uses for that kind of file. Anything you are taking away instead — a statement, a register, a spreadsheet export — still offers the share sheet, because that is the right thing there.

My Interviews now carries a red count in the menu, so a round booked with you announces itself instead of waiting to be found. It counts the rounds you have not written up yet.

Course videos no longer have a size limit. A lesson can be as long as you need; a large file is sent up in pieces rather than turned away at 100 MB.

When you are putting questions inside a course video, you now get a bar showing the whole lesson with a yellow marker wherever a question sits, so you can see at a glance whether they are spread through it or bunched at the start. Tap a marker to jump to that question. A question pinned past the end of the video is marked in red, because the learner would only ever meet it once the video had finished.

And when a learner gets one of those questions wrong, the video now takes them back to the question before it and plays that stretch again — the part that holds the answer — instead of simply asking them to guess again.
